project_title: How Football Clubs Reveal Market Preferences Through Transfer Spending

core_framework.price_role: Transfer fee as revealed willingness to pay

charts.title: Data Understanding Dashboard
charts.main_insight: The database has enough role, league, ability and price coverage to support STP-based market analysis.
charts.marketing_interpretation: This chart establishes the market research foundation: players can be segmented by role, league context and valuation variables.
charts.speaker_note: Use this briefly to prove that the analysis is not anecdotal; it has enough structured variables for marketing interpretation.

charts.title: Price Skewness: Star-Driven Premium Market
charts.main_insight: Football transfer value is extremely right-skewed, with a small elite segment dominating total market value.
charts.marketing_interpretation: The market behaves like a premium star economy where symbolic value, scarcity and attention concentrate price at the top.
charts.recommended_slide: Opening: why transfer price is a marketing question
charts.speaker_note: This is the hook: transfer pricing looks like a premium product market, not a normal uniform labor market.

charts.title: Youth / Growth Positioning Map
charts.main_insight: Young high-potential players occupy disproportionate high-value zones.
charts.marketing_interpretation: Clubs position these players as future-growth assets rather than merely current-performance players.
charts.recommended_slide: Growth Positioning: youth and future value
charts.speaker_note: Explain that the club is buying an option on future value, resale value and brand story.

charts.title: League / Brand Positioning: Median Price Ladder
charts.main_insight: Top leagues form a visible market-value ladder.
charts.marketing_interpretation: League identity acts like a brand label that signals quality, reduces uncertainty and frames willingness to pay.
charts.recommended_slide: Brand Positioning: league identity and brand equity
charts.speaker_note: Use this to translate league differences into brand equity rather than only football strength.

charts.title: Entertainment / Attention Positioning Map
charts.chart_type: scatter with density contour and trend line
charts.main_insight: Entertainment-oriented player profiles show a positive price gradient.
charts.marketing_interpretation: Attacking spectacle, dribbling, speed and reputation turn players into attention-generating assets.
charts.recommended_slide: Attention Positioning: entertainment and visibility premium
charts.speaker_note: Connect football highlights to attention economy: the player is both product and promotional asset.

charts.title: PCA Archetype Map: Price Gradient
charts.main_insight: High-value players concentrate in clearer latent archetype regions.
charts.marketing_interpretation: The market buys recognizable player archetypes, not isolated individual attributes.
charts.speaker_note: Frame PCA as a marketing perceptual map: it shows where player-products sit in the market mind.

charts.title: PCA Archetypes by Position and League Brand
charts.main_insight: Position and league context structure the archetype map.
charts.marketing_interpretation: Player role defines product category, while league context adds brand meaning.
charts.speaker_note: Use if time allows after the PCA price map; it explains why position and league are not just controls.

charts.title: t-SNE Identity Maps
charts.main_insight: Player identities cluster into neighborhoods, and price premiums appear in selected neighborhoods.
charts.marketing_interpretation: Clubs compare players within identity-based consideration sets, not across the entire market at once.
charts.recommended_slide: How the market organizes player identities
charts.speaker_note: This is the visual proof that the market has neighborhoods of substitutable but differentiated products.

charts.title: Marketing Positioning Maps
charts.main_insight: Growth, brand and attention each show a relationship with price from different angles.
charts.marketing_interpretation: This is the integrated STP view: clubs price multiple positioning dimensions simultaneously.
charts.speaker_note: Use this as the strategic summary chart before moving to segmentation and price model.

charts.title: Segmentation: Market Segments and Segment DNA
charts.main_insight: Player profiles can be grouped into meaningful market segments with different price logic.
charts.marketing_interpretation: This operationalizes STP segmentation by naming player groups as market categories rather than just football roles.
charts.speaker_note: Translate each segment into a value proposition: growth asset, creative connector, utility value.

charts.title: Implicit Market Premiums
charts.main_insight: Quality, growth, brand and attention signals translate into measurable price premiums.
charts.marketing_interpretation: The model converts positioning narratives into revealed willingness-to-pay language.
charts.recommended_slide: Transfer fee as revealed willingness to pay
charts.speaker_note: Do not present this as prediction accuracy; present it as a premium decomposition.

charts.title: Paid Transfer Premium Heatmap
charts.main_insight: Actual paid fees vary across age-role combinations.
charts.marketing_interpretation: This validates that positioning logic appears in observed buying behavior, not only estimated market value.
charts.speaker_note: Use near the end to show that the argument is grounded in actual paid transfer fees.

charts.title: Growth Positioning by Age Segment
charts.main_insight: Age lifecycle segments have different price distributions and upside ceilings.
charts.marketing_interpretation: This clarifies youth as a lifecycle positioning variable rather than a simple age effect.
charts.speaker_note: Use this if the audience needs a clearer distribution view after the bubble map.

charts.title: Brand Positioning: League × Role Price Surface
charts.main_insight: League brand and player role jointly shape median valuation.
charts.marketing_interpretation: Brand premium is not uniform; it interacts with player product category.
charts.speaker_note: Use as a stronger version of league-brand interpretation when discussing role differences.

charts.title: Segment Archetype Radar
charts.main_insight: Market segments differ by value proposition, not only by price.
charts.marketing_interpretation: Each segment sells a different bundle of benefits: quality, upside, attention or brand access.
charts.speaker_note: This chart helps convert clustering into marketing language.

charts.title: Integrated STP Positioning Map
charts.main_insight: Premium players often sit where future potential and attention value overlap.
charts.marketing_interpretation: This is the clearest consulting-style map of growth positioning versus attention positioning.
charts.speaker_note: Use this as a final visual synthesis before the conclusion.

charts.title: League Transfer Flow Heatmap
charts.main_insight: Transfer capital flows toward stronger league brands and high-demand markets.
charts.marketing_interpretation: This provides light differentiated-competition intuition without making scarcity the core story.
charts.speaker_note: Keep this as optional support; avoid turning the project into auction theory.

charts.title: Premium Overlap: Super-Premium Player Identities
charts.chart_type: bar chart plus bubble positioning map
charts.main_insight: Growth, brand and attention premiums often stack on the same player identities, creating super-premium profiles.
charts.marketing_interpretation: The market does not reward isolated signals equally; it disproportionately rewards players who combine future narrative, elite-league brand assurance and visibility value.
charts.speaker_note: Use this as the narrative turning point: the three premiums are not separate stories; they converge on the same marketable player identities.

presentation_outline.slide_title: Why transfer price is a marketing question
presentation_outline.objective: Open with price as revealed preference.
presentation_outline.key_message: Transfer fees reveal what clubs value.
presentation_outline.speaker_note: Start from the skewed market to show that this is a premium positioning market.

presentation_outline.slide_title: Course framework mapping: 5C to STP to Price
presentation_outline.objective: Anchor the project in marketing models.
presentation_outline.key_message: Players, clubs and leagues form a structured market system.
presentation_outline.speaker_note: Keep this concise; the main model is STP.

presentation_outline.objective: Show youth and potential as future-value positioning.
presentation_outline.key_message: The market prices future narratives, not just current performance.
presentation_outline.speaker_note: Use chart_03 as the main visual; chart_13 is backup detail.

presentation_outline.objective: Show league identity as brand equity.
presentation_outline.key_message: League identity functions like a quality label.
presentation_outline.speaker_note: Translate league effects into brand and risk-reduction language.

presentation_outline.objective: Show entertainment value as marketable attention.
presentation_outline.speaker_note: Explain that attacking stars are both on-field products and media assets.

presentation_outline.objective: Move beyond descriptive stats into multivariate identity.
presentation_outline.key_message: The market prices recognizable player identities.
presentation_outline.speaker_note: Use PCA first, then t-SNE if time allows.

presentation_outline.objective: Name player groups as market segments.
presentation_outline.key_message: Different player segments sell different value propositions.
presentation_outline.speaker_note: Connect clusters to club strategy and budget constraints.

presentation_outline.objective: Connect the narrative to revealed willingness to pay.
presentation_outline.key_message: Quality, growth, brand and attention become implicit premiums.
presentation_outline.speaker_note: Avoid formal econometrics; focus on premium interpretation.

presentation_outline.objective: Show that youth, brand and attention premiums stack on the same player identities.
presentation_outline.key_message: Modern football markets create super-premium player identities by stacking future narrative, brand assurance and visibility value.
presentation_outline.speaker_note: This is the key turning point from separate evidence to unified conclusion.

presentation_outline.key_message: Premium players combine future potential and attention value.
presentation_outline.speaker_note: This is the strongest final visual before conclusion.

presentation_outline.objective: Use actual transactions and flows as support.
presentation_outline.key_message: Actual payments and capital flows support the positioning story.
presentation_outline.speaker_note: Keep this secondary. Do not center scarcity premium.

presentation_outline.key_message: Transfer fee is the price of positioning under uncertainty.
presentation_outline.speaker_note: End with growth, brand and attention as the three premiums.

excluded_from_main_story.reason: Scarcity premium is useful only as light differentiated-competition intuition. It should not be a core insight because it shifts the project toward economics / auction theory rather than STP-based marketing positioning.
